prompt: Segment the chronic stroke lesion in the T1-weighted image of sub-M2213 (ds004884/ARC, OpenNeuro), producing a binary lesion mask in native T1w space.
reference: Expert manual lesion tracing (ARC), rigid-registered from native T2w into T1w space.
threshold_basis: FIXED (literature): full=0.70 at manual-tracing inter-rater ceiling on T1w (Dice 0.727; Tavenner et al. 2023, Front Neuroimaging 1:1098604, doi:10.3389/fnimg.2022.1098604). pass=0.50 near automated SOTA on ATLAS v2.0 (Dice ~0.50-0.58; Deb et al. 2023, BeSt-LeS, arXiv:2310.07060). Population: chronic-stroke T1w manual tracing (ATLAS v2.0; Liew et al. 2022, Sci Data 9:320, doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01401-7). Single subject -> no LOTO envelope.
references: Tavenner BP, Donnelly MR, Barisano G, Liew S-L. Front Neuroimaging 1:1098604, 2023. doi:10.3389/fnimg.2022.1098604 (inter-rater manual-tracing Dice 0.727, T1w).
Liew S-L, Tavenner BP, Donnelly MR, et al. ATLAS v2.0. Sci Data 9:320, 2022. doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01401-7 (chronic-stroke T1w manual-lesion dataset).
Deb P, Baru LB, Dadi K, S BR. BeSt-LeS. MICCAI BrainLes 2023, arXiv:2310.07060 (automated SOTA on ATLAS v2.0, Dice ~0.50-0.58).

weight_basis.lesion_f1: lesion_f1 lowered from 0.30 to 0.10 and the weight given to dice. Every subject in this task carries exactly one expert lesion, so detection F1 can only report 'found it' or 'did not' -- which dice already covers. At 0.30 it also made a single stray voxel in a submission cost ~12 quality points, because the metric counts a one-voxel component as a whole false lesion. This is a policy choice, not a calibrated threshold: with one expert tracing there is no inter-rater disagreement to derive one from.
weight_basis.min_lesion_voxels: Components below 10 voxels are not counted as lesion instances, on either side. The reference is registered from the T2w the expert drew on into T1w space, and nearest-neighbour resampling of a rigid rotation severs thin connections: across the five subjects this leaves 14 stray pieces of 1-6 voxels, while the smallest real lesion is 26672 voxels. Counting those pieces as lesions made a perfect segmentation score lesion_f1 0.18 on sub-M2213, penalised for missing nine lesions the resampling had created. Any cut between 6 and 26672 gives the same result here, so the exact value is not load-bearing; 10 matches the rule used in subjects.tsv to separate a speck from a lesion. It applies to submissions too, which is the stray-voxel tolerance a segmentation tool needs.

lesion_f1_basis: DERIVED (arithmetic, not a tuned threshold). Every subject in this task carries exactly one expert lesion, so with that lesion found and k spurious components lesion_f1 = 2/(2+k): 1.00 at k=0, 0.67 at k=1, 0.50 at k=2. full = 1.0 therefore means 'found it, nothing spurious' and pass = 0.5 means 'at most two spurious components', with min_lesion_voxels = 10 already removing resampling debris. The metric cannot take intermediate values here, so these are the only two meaningful settings rather than a calibration. It carries weight 0.1 for the same reason -- see weight_basis.
